claims.text: Inverse-model-guided, high-alkalinity continuous-solvothermal synthesis can steer a multi-element alloy catalyst toward a Cu–Pt-enriched surface configuration.
The Cu–Pt-enriched configuration will simultaneously improve low-temperature oxidation activity, poisoning resistance, and durability after severe ageing.
The initial candidates are fresh, 1 wt% multi-element alloy catalysts made from up to 19 metal precursors on La-doped γ-Al2O3.
The initial catalysts contain agglomerates of fine metallic particles.
Synthesis at 200–350 °C with 25 M NaOH and controlled pressure favors Cu–Pt surface rearrangement.
Post-ageing electronic and atomic reconstruction forms electronically coupled Cu–Pt cooperative adsorption sites.
The intervention creates beneficial alloy/support interfacial states.
The intervention limits detrimental phase segregation and excessive incorporation of Fe, Ni, and Cu into La–Al mixed oxides.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites weaken excessively strong CO binding.
Cu–Pt surface rearrangement improves redox buffering and oxygen mobility.
Improved adsorption and redox properties couple efficient hydrocarbon oxidation with NO reduction.
Cu–Pt surface rearrangement avoids the electronic isolation of Pt caused by Pt coordination with Ni or Fe.
The proposed mechanism lowers light-off temperature and increases overall conversion.
After severe ageing, the targeted formulation will have a T50 at least 5 °C lower than the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark and catalysts produced with random synthesis parameters.
After severe ageing, the targeted formulation will improve conversion at 350 °C by at least 2 percentage points relative to the stated comparators.
The claimed performance applies after ageing at 900 °C for 5 h under cyclic lean/rich, water-containing, near-stoichiometric exhaust conditions.
The claimed performance applies during testing from 100 to 500 °C at a 10 °C min−1 ramp in a feed containing NO, CO, C3H6, i-C5H12, CO2, O2, H2, and N2.
The hypothesis is restricted to the explored five- to nineteen-element, 1 wt% supported-catalyst space and may not translate quantitatively outside the defined ageing and exhaust conditions.

contradictions.description: The requested change relative to the unmodified catalyst is not defined. The prediction and falsification rule instead compare the targeted catalyst with Pd/Al2O3 and randomly selected formulations, which are not necessarily composition-matched unmodified controls.

The hypothesis claims improved poisoning resistance and lifetime durability, but the quantitative outcome and falsification rule address only post-ageing light-off/conversion and Cu–Pt enrichment; they provide no poison-challenge threshold or vehicle-lifetime durability criterion.
